# 1: Project Overview

Analysis of my health data while doing archaeology in Southern Italy during July 2025 and June 2026. This will be looking at factors such as my heart rate data, step count, and the temperature of the local area. This project will also compare my health data to weather data, such as seeing if there is a correlation between heart rate and weather data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2: Data Sources

The first data source is my personal health data from the Google Health App, and the other is weather information at Torre Mordillo from Open Meteo.

## 2.1 Summary of sources

My physical activity data, including heart rate, calories, and respiratory rate was downloaded from my Google Health account. The data was collected by my Sense 2 Fitbit watch.

```{r source-summary, echo=FALSE}
sources <- tribble(
  ~Source,            ~Producer,          ~Format,  ~Coverage,          ~Using,
  "Google Health",    "Google Health",   "CSV",  "FitBit watch, 2018-2026",   "Yes",
  "Open Meteo",    "Open-Meteo GmbH",   "CSV",  "Torre Mordillo, 2025-2026",   "Yes",
  "Meteo Blue",    "Meteo BLue",   "CSV",  "Spezzano Albanese, 2025-2026",   "No, see 2.3"
)

knitr::kable(sources)
```

## 2.2.1: Google Health Data

**Producer and authority.** The data was collected by Fitbit, and later Google Health. It is not public data by default (thought users can publish their own health data collected if they so choose. This data is my own dataset that I have full legal authority over, and I am using it for a class project.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The data was collected by my Fitbit watch into the Fitbit app (which later merged with Google Health) so that I, the user, can see my health data and compare it to past data.

**Collection method.** The data was collected by my Fitbit watch via sensor. The data was collected by my Sense 2 Fitbit watch using built in sensors that monitor heart rate, skin temperature and more.

**Coverage and resolution.** The time period I will be filtering for in my personal health data is July 2026 and June 2025, which is the time period I was in Southern Italy, however in the raw files contain data from 2018 until late October 2026. The data include multiple types of units, such as bpm, steps, milliseconds, days, and calories.

**Licence.** As it is my own data, I do not need to worry about a license to use it for my own personal project. I give people a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International license for my data (CC BY NC-ND 4.0) as I do not want people profiting off my data.

**Access.** Anyone with the same or similar type of watch can access their data by downloading it from their account. Specifics on how to do that likely varies depending on which company holds the data.

**Known problems.** The data is only collected when I wear my watch, meaning that there are many instances of missing data. Additionally, the sensors sometimes get confused, such as counting me tapping my hand as steps.

## 2.2.2 Open Meteo

**Producer and authority.** Made by Patrick by Open Meteo GmbH. It aggregate existing open weather datasets and combines them to give more accurate data. It was published to give peopl access to open source weather data.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** Open source weather and climate data for researchers to use.

**Collection method.** Collected from 30 different national and international weather models.

**Coverage and resolution.** Open Meteo has worldwide coverage and high resolution weather models, however I specifically am only looking at the weather at Torre Mordillo in specific months in the summers of 2025 and 2026.

**Licence.** Open source, API data offered under Attribution International (CC BY 4.0).

**Access.** I got it by downloading from the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API webpage (https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api), and picking the time period, and the specific longitude and latitude.

**Known problems.** I chose the variables I wanted for the file when downloading from the website, I may want different variables later on, meaning I would have to re-download the file(s).

# 3: Licensing and permissions

## 3.1: Licence by source

```{r licence-table, echo=FALSE}

  ~Source,          ~Licence,                    ~Attribution_required, ~Attribution_given,

)

knitr::kable(licences)
```

## 3.2: Unresolved licensing

None.

## 3.3: Downstream permissions

The weather data is open source, with a Attribution International (CC BY 4.0) license. I give my own data non-commercial use only, as I don't mind people seeing the data, but I do not want people profiting off of it or using it without my permission. Since I downloaded the weather data for free, that means I can use it for non-commercial use. This means that any combined data from my personal data and weather data also is for non-commercial use.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4: Consent and identifiability

The weather data does not describe people. My personal health data only describes myself

**Consent.** The health data is my own, and as I am the one analysing it, I consented to put any information included in this project. It was collected via sensors on my Fitbit Sense 2 watch. I consented to this data collection when I started wearing Fitbit watches. This data was then extracted from the Google Health App by specifically requesting it.

**Identifiability.** The health data collected is from one person (myself). The project is only looking at one person, and not a population.

**How sensitive data will be used.** Sensitive data was taken out of my health data before I uploaded it to this project, such as any identifying information like email address and other profile information. The data folder I received from Google Health contained many subfolders, but I elected to only use the physical activity subfolder as that was what was relevant to the research, and also did not contain any sensitive information about me.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5: Exclusions and harms

## 5.1: Excluded data from the audit

I will be removing any data outside of specific time periods (likely any time that is no July 2025 and June 2026 data) as I am focusing my project on those specific time periods. Other data excluded is any personally identifying information about me such as email both for privacy reasons and because it is not relevant to the project. Excluding data outside of particular time periods means I cannot use them to compare data to other time periods.

## 5.2: Who could be harmed

Someone could misuse this data to make an analysis of my health and me as a person without my permission.

## 5.3: Unreleased working data

I would not publish any data that is not from the specific period's in time that I am analysing (i.e. when I was doing archaeology, and any other periods of time I may use to compare against) as it is not relevant to the project.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 6: Data Stewardship

**Where it lives.** My personal health data and the weather data will be on the Github repository. This repository will likely not be touched after December.

**Who maintains it.** \[If nobody, say nobody\] My personal health data will not be updated after this class project ends. The weather data will also not be updated, as I will only be analysing specific time periods. Open Meteo may update the weather data for the specific time and place I am analysing, however that it highly unlikely and would be updated on their website, not in this repository.

**Formats and dependencies.** Both my personal health data and the weather data are in csv files and will be possible to open at any point. None of the files have any dependencies.

**Lifespan.** \[How long is this meaningfully usable before it needs updating or should be retired?\] The data I'm looking it is contained to specific periods of time, and therefore will not be updated. My raw health information contains data up until October 2026, and any data analysis for a time period after that cannot be done.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 7: Use of AI

I have not used any AI models in this project.

**AI log:** /log/`AI-LOG.md` — maintained from 3 November 2026 and committed alongside each stage of work.

No AI has been used in this project. Data was extracted either from the Google Health app, or the Open Meteo website without the use of AI. Code in the Analysis.R file was written with the help of code from class, Stack Overflow or websites such as w3schools.com and geeksforgeeks.com
